On October 11, our team visited families whose tents had been burned, leaving them without shelter once again. Even as we filmed, heavy gunfire echoed around us. This is the reality of life in Gaza. Families who have lost everything continue to live under the threat of violence, yet refuse to be driven from their land. This is what steadfastness looks like. Sumud. A determination that is difficult to comprehend unless you understand what it means to face the loss of your homeland. They have burned their shelters, destroyed their neighborhoods, and displaced them again and again. But they have not broken their connection to Palestine. They are not leaving. What Is Palestine? Palestine is a historical term for a region that has encompassed many territories — originally named by the Romans in 135 AD, when they renamed Judea in an attempt to sever the Jewish connection to the land. Across the centuries, the land was ruled by empire after empire, yet no sovereign country called Palestine ever existed. It began as a name meant to erase a people — and the question today is whether it's still being used to do exactly that. The last episode of "What Is" Season 1 is this Thursday at 11am ET.

Palestinian farmers and Israeli peace activists joined together Friday to harvest olives in Bethlehem in the occupied West Bank, despite ongoing tensions and threats of violence from Israeli settlers. Volunteers from the Israeli-Palestinian peace group Combatants for Peace helped local farmers gather olives on land surrounded by Israeli settlements, while Israeli soldiers patrolled the area. Chen Alon, an Israeli co-founder of the organization and former Israel Defense Forces soldier, said the joint harvest was intended to show solidarity with Palestinian farmers amid settler attacks and accused Israeli forces of supporting the violence. The United Nations has documented nearly 200 settler attacks linked to the olive harvest since September.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered the army there to prepare for a full closure of the occupied West Bank after suspected gunmen shot and killed two Israeli soldiers. Video from the Israeli army showed the firefight at a military checkpoint on Friday. The two attackers, both Palestinian, were killed in the exchange of gunfire. The army said it prevented the men from advancing towards civilians. Following the shoot-out, Netanyahu blamed Hamas for the attack and vowed that Israel would retaliate. “We will act, first of all, to demolish this place, to change it completely,” Netanyahu said. “We will evacuate the residents. We will go house by house. We will also remove the weapons there, and all the terror infrastructure will be dealt with and destroyed.” After his comments, construction equipment could be seen starting to demolish homes near the site of the shooting.
